title: Low-Rank Compression of Language Models Via Gradient-Based Rank Selection

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution aims to solve per-layer rank selection for low-rank (SVD) LLM compression without requiring post-compression fine-tuning, jointly optimizing compression rate and downstream accuracy across layers. Paper [2] explicitly addresses the problem of determining the optimal rank for each layer in neural network compression, describing it as a mixed discrete-continuous optimization problem. Paper [6] also tackles joint rank selection for low-rank compression, emphasizing efficient rank-selection methods. Both papers share the same objective at the problem-class level: optimizing per-layer rank selection for low-rank compression. Therefore, the purpose is **covered**.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves applying SVD to each target weight matrix, inserting a learnable masking layer in the reconstruction, and training only the mask parameters on a small calibration set to progressively increase compression while minimizing divergence of intermediate activations from the original model. Paper [5] uses SVD for LLM compression but focuses on truncation-aware singular value selection and updating compressed weights, which differs from the learnable masking approach. Paper [9] discusses learning pruning masks with stochastic optimization, which is conceptually similar to the learnable masking layer but operates in a different context (pruning rather than rank selection). No prior paper combines SVD with learnable masking layers and total-variation loss for contiguous singular-value selection. Thus, the mechanism is **uncovered**.

### Evaluation
The evaluation uses a calibration set of 3,000 documents and compares performance against fine-tuning-free rank-selection baselines (STRS, ARS, LLM-Pruner) on Llama-2-7B/13B, Llama-3-8B, and Gemma-7B for common-sense reasoning and open-domain QA. Papers [2], [5], and [6] all evaluate rank-selection methods for low-rank compression using standard benchmarks and metrics, such as accuracy improvements on downstream tasks. While the specific datasets and models differ, the evaluation design (benchmark-based comparison of rank-selection methods) is substantively equivalent. Therefore, the evaluation is **covered**.

### Domain
The domain is LLM compression via low-rank decomposition. Papers [3], [5], and [6] explicitly address LLM compression using low-rank methods, making this application area well-established. Although the contribution targets specific models (e.g., Llama-2-13B, Llama-3-8B), this is a change of instance, not a new domain. Thus, the domain is **covered**.

**PURPOSE: Solve per-layer rank selection for low-rank (SVD) LLM compression without any post-compression fine-tuning, jointly optimizing compression rate and downstream accuracy across layers.**

Paper [2] explicitly addresses "determining what the optimal rank of each layer is" for neural net compression, described as "an architecture search problem with one hyperparameter per layer" with "a mixed discrete-continuous optimization jointly over the ranks." Paper [3] addresses "low-rank compression of LLMs" with focus on "the key to low-rank compression lies in low-rank factorization" and rank selection. Paper [5] addresses SVD-based LLM compression. However, the specific constraint of *no post-compression fine-tuning* is a distinguishing element — paper [5] explicitly notes "lack of update on the compressed weights after SVD truncation" as a limitation it tries to address (meaning it does use updates). Paper [2] is about general neural nets with training involved. The closest match to the fine-tuning-free joint rank selection purpose for LLMs is paper [3], which applies Bayesian optimization to rank selection in LLMs. But the "without fine-tuning" constraint is central. Paper [5] covers SVD LLM compression but uses weight updates. The purpose at the problem-class level — "jointly select per-layer ranks for SVD compression to optimize accuracy" — is covered by [2] and [3].

---

**MECHANISM: SVD on weight matrices + learnable masking layer in reconstruction + train only mask parameters on calibration set + progressive compression + TV loss for contiguous singular-value selection.**

Paper [12] (SMCP) uses soft masking during pruning to allow pruned channels to adaptively return — a learnable mask trained during compression. Paper [9] studies "learning pruning masks by optimizing the expected loss of stochastic pruning masks." Paper [23] uses differentiable/learnable structure search for pruning. However, none of these combine: (1) SVD decomposition specifically, (2) a masking layer inserted into the SVD reconstruction, (3) training only mask parameters on a calibration set, (4) TV loss for contiguous singular value selection. The TV loss for encouraging contiguous selection of singular values is a distinctive primitive not found in any prior paper. The combination of SVD + learnable mask + TV regularization for contiguous selection appears genuinely absent. Paper [5] uses SVD for LLMs but with weight updates and truncation-aware data whitening, not a masking layer with TV loss. No prior paper combines these specific primitives.

**EVALUATION: Calibration set of 3,000 documents; comparison against fine-tuning-free baselines (STRS, ARS, LLM-Pruner) on Llama-2/3, Gemma on commonsense reasoning and open-domain QA benchmarks.**

The evaluation design uses standard NLP benchmarks (MMLU, BoolQ, OpenbookQA, NQ-Open, PIQA) — a well-established benchmark family for LLM evaluation. Papers [3] and [5] both evaluate SVD-based LLM compression on standard LLM benchmarks with similar metrics. The design of "evaluate compressed LLM on commonsense reasoning / QA benchmarks, compare against baselines at fixed compression ratios" is used in [3] and [5]. This is a covered evaluation design.

---

**DOMAIN: LLM compression / low-rank decomposition.**

Papers [3] and [5] both work in LLM compression via low-rank/SVD decomposition. This domain is clearly covered.

### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to escape the restriction of prior methods that keep only the top-k singular values (magnitude-ordered), enabling more flexible compression. Paper [19] discusses truncation-aware singular value decomposition for LLM compression, which addresses the issue of truncating smaller singular values leading to higher compression loss. While [19] focuses on improving compression by addressing truncation, it does not explicitly aim to escape the restriction of top-k singular values or enable "any-k" selection. No other paper explicitly addresses this purpose.  
**Conclusion:** NONE.

---

### Mechanism
The contribution introduces a learnable singular-value masking linear parameter vector that selects the best "any-k" singular values in a fine-tuning-free setting. Paper [19] uses SVD for LLM compression but focuses on truncation-aware methods and updating compressed weights post-SVD truncation, which differs from the learnable masking mechanism here. Paper [2] discusses learning matrix singular values with neural networks, but it does not propose a masking mechanism for "any-k" selection. Paper [3] introduces sparse learnable masks for feature selection, which is conceptually similar to the masking mechanism but operates in a different context (feature selection, not singular value selection). Despite the conceptual similarity, no prior paper directly matches the mechanism of learnable singular-value masking for "any-k" selection.  
**Conclusion:** NONE.

---

### Evaluation
The evaluation includes ablations analyzing the TV loss contribution and demonstrates practical performance improvements from selectively reducing individual-layer ranks. Paper [23] uses total variation regularization in spectral unmixing, which matches the use of TV loss as a regularization term. Paper [12] discusses layer-selective rank reduction in LLMs, which aligns with the evaluation's focus on selectively reducing individual-layer ranks. Paper [19] evaluates SVD-based compression methods for LLMs, including layer-wise rank allocation, which is consistent with the evaluation design here. These prior papers collectively cover the evaluation design, even though the specific benchmarks and objects differ.  
**Conclusion:** [12], [19], [23].

---

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of LLM compression and low-rank decomposition. Papers [1], [5], [11], [12], and [19] all address LLM compression or low-rank decomposition, making this domain well-covered.  
**Conclusion:** [1], [5], [11], [12], [19].

**PURPOSE: Escape the restriction of top-k (magnitude-ordered) singular value selection, enabling more flexible/any-k compression.**

Paper [12] (LASER) demonstrates that "selectively removing higher-order components" (i.e., removing top singular values, not just keeping them) improves LLM performance — this directly motivates escaping the top-k restriction. Paper [18] discusses learned subproblem selection. Paper [1] discusses adaptive low-rank compression of LLMs. However, the specific purpose of "enabling any-k selection beyond magnitude-ordered top-k" is most directly addressed by [12], which shows that keeping top-k by magnitude is suboptimal and that selective rank reduction (including removing high-magnitude components) improves performance. This is substantively equivalent to the purpose of escaping top-k magnitude ordering. Paper [19] (SVD-LLM) also notes that "truncating smaller singular values may lead to higher compression loss," implicitly motivating non-magnitude-ordered selection.

**MECHANISM: Learnable singular-value masking via a linear parameter vector that selects any-k singular values in a fine-tuning-free setting; lighter than ARS (RNN/GRU-based).**

Paper [3] (SLM) proposes "Sparse Learnable Masks" for end-to-end feature selection — a learnable sparse mask that selects which features to keep. This is the same primitive (learnable binary/soft mask over a set of components) applied to a different domain. However, SLM is for feature selection in general ML, not singular value selection. Paper [6] addresses learning/updating singular values via optimization. Paper [7] covers singular value thresholding. None of the prior papers describe a learnable linear masking vector specifically over singular values for LLM compression in a fine-tuning-free setting. The combination of (a) learnable mask, (b) applied to singular values, (c) fine-tuning-free, (d) any-k selection is not covered. Paper [3]'s learnable sparse mask is the closest primitive match at the mechanism level.

**EVALUATION: Ablations on TV loss contribution; any-k vs top-k comparison; per-layer rank analysis across architectures.**

Paper [12] performs per-layer rank reduction analysis and shows layer-selective rank reduction improves 0-shot performance — directly matching the "selectively reducing individual-layer ranks can improve 0-shot performance" finding cited as consistent with Sharma et al. 2024. Paper [1] performs ablations on LLM compression components. The evaluation design (ablation of loss components, per-layer analysis, 0-shot benchmark evaluation) is a standard design used across multiple prior papers [1], [12], [19]. The "TV loss ablation" is a specific component ablation, and per-layer rank analysis appears in [12] and [19].

**DOMAIN: LLM compression / low-rank decomposition.**

Papers [1], [5], [12], [18], [19] all work in LLM compression with low-rank decomposition. This domain is clearly covered.
